name: tar
tasks: list what is in an archive

examples.does: Pack a folder into a gzip-compressed archive
List what is inside, without unpacking
Unpack into another folder (it must exist)
Use zstd: much faster than gzip at similar size

pitfalls: Unpacking over existing files replaces them. List first (-t), unpack into an empty folder.
tar drops the leading / from names, so restoring with -C / puts files back in place.

name: gzip

examples.does: Compress to big.log.gz and keep the original
Read a compressed log without unpacking it
Check that the file is not damaged

pitfalls: Without -k, gzip replaces the original with the .gz file.

name: zip
pitfalls: zip does not keep Linux owners and permissions well; use tar for server backups.

name: sha256sum
summary: Checksums: is a file exactly the one that was sent
tasks: check a transfer into the air-gapped network

examples.does: Save the checksum to send along with the file
Check the file against the saved checksum: OK or FAILED

pitfalls: Get the checksum through a different path than the file, or a tampered file can come with a matching checksum.
